key_insight: A psychiatry-specific large language model may help clinicians interpret complex patient narratives more consistently, supporting more standardized and higher-quality psychiatric care. The main idea is that AI can augment—not replace—clinical decision making in a highly heterogeneous domain.
problem_solved: Psychiatric care often relies on unstructured, longitudinal patient narratives, which are difficult to interpret consistently across clinicians. This leads to variability in assessments and treatment decisions, making standardization and quality improvement challenging.
method: Develop or evaluate a psychiatry-specific large language model tailored to clinical psychiatric language and context.
Use the model to assist with interpreting longitudinal narrative data from patient records or clinical notes.
Compare how AI-supported interpretation may improve consistency and support clinician decision making in psychiatric care.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper highlights a high-value application of domain-specific LLMs in a sensitive clinical setting. It shows how carefully designed AI tools can augment expert judgment, improve consistency, and potentially make care more scalable and reliable.

paper_title: Towards AI-augmented decision making in psychiatry
